item.title: Ukraine wants peace but won't give in, Zelenskiy says on Independence Day
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelenskiy made a defiant speech marking Independence Day celebrations.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Ukraine wants peace but will not just give in to Russia at any price, President Volodymyr Zelenskiy said on Monday in a defiant speech marking Independence Day celebrations. British Prime Minister Andy Burnham and European Council President Antonio Costa were among foreign leaders and dignitaries who arrived in Kyiv for events on the 35th anniversary of Ukraine's break from the Soviet Union. Burnham was scheduled to co-chair a meeting of the "Coalition of the Willing" - a group of countries backing Ukraine - later on Monday during his first visit to the Ukrainian capital as prime minister. "Ukraine absolutely wants peace, but it's not ready to simply surrender," Zelenskiy said in a video posted on Telegram showing him standing in a traditional Ukrainian embroidered shirt in the square in front of the golden-domed St Michael's monastery in Kyiv where burned-out Russian tanks are on show. He said Russia's demand - repeatedly rejected by Ukraine - that Kyiv cede the remaining part of the eastern Donbas area that is not in Russian hands after 4-1/2 years of war would not be enough to stop Russian aggression. "We will not let them (Russians) seize the initiative, deceive Europe and the entire world into thinking that we simply need to give up Donbas and everything will be over soon," he said. Hundreds of thousands of people have been killed, and swathes of Ukrainian territory have been laid waste, since Russia launched its full-scale invasion on February 24, 2022. U.S.-led peace talks to bring a lasting end to the war stalled earlier this year as Ukraine refused Russia's demands to cede more territory, and fighting rages along a 750-mile (1,200-km) frontline. TRIBUTE TO UKRAINIAN PEOPLE Russia's advances on the battlefield have slowed this year and Ukraine has recaptured some land in the southeast. However, Moscow's forces are threatening the strategic eastern city of Kostiantynivka in the eastern region of Donetsk - which forms part of Donbas, together with the Luhansk region. Exploiting Ukraine's critical shortage of anti-ballistic missiles, Russia has also stepped up its campaign of air strikes at cities far from the front line this summer. Ukraine has also increased its long-range attacks on Russian refineries and logistics infrastructure, aimed at undermining Moscow's war effort. Paying tribute to the people and soldiers defending Ukraine in the war, Zelenskiy also called on allies to give it "everything" needed to stop the war. Urging them to bring Russia to the negotiating table and hit it with more sanctions, Zelenskiy said he hoped that "all the contradictions and fears" the United States has regarding Russia will disappear. "China must no longer remain silent," he added. Other dignitaries present for the celebrations included Luxembourg Prime Minister Luc Frieden, Moldova's President Maia Sandu and Estonia's President Alar Karis, Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on X, posting photos of the officials arriving at the Kyiv station.

item.title: Irán amenaza con multas y detención a los buques que violen las normas en el estrecho de Ormuz
item.description: Irán ha advertido de que los buques que incumplan sus disposiciones relativas al tránsito por el estrecho de Ormuz podrían enfrentarse a restricciones, como multas, detención o confiscación, según ha informado la Autoridad del Estrecho del Golfo Pérsico en una publicación en la red social X.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Irán ha advertido de que los buques que incumplan sus disposiciones relativas al tránsito por el estrecho de Ormuz podrían enfrentarse a restricciones, como multas, detención o confiscación, según ha informado la Autoridad del Estrecho del Golfo Pérsico en una publicación en la red social X. La advertencia aumenta los riesgos para los fletadores y armadores cuyos buques transitan por el estrecho de Ormuz, una vía navegable clave para los transportes energéticos mundiales. La Autoridad del Estrecho del Golfo Pérsico, un nuevo organismo creado por Irán con el objetivo de gestionar el estrecho, ha indicado que los propietarios de la carga deben consultar una lista actualizada de buques considerados no conformes para los viajes relacionados con el golfo Pérsico. Los buques que realicen operaciones, como trasvases de barco a barco o transbordos, con buques no conformes también se añadirán a la lista de restricción, según se indicó. Los buques que deseen que se elimine su nombre de la lista de buques no conformes deberán presentar una solicitud con las explicaciones pertinentes a las autoridades marítimas iraníes, según la publicación.

item.title: Six countries want EU talks in September on taxing windfall profits of oil companies
item.description: Six European Union countries want the 27-nation EU to discuss in September a mechanism to tax windfall profits of oil companies triggered by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, a letter by their finance ministers showed on Monday.
item.dc:creator: Jan Strupczewski
item.content:encoded: Six European Union countries want the 27-nation EU to discuss in September a mechanism to tax windfall profits of oil companies triggered by Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz, a letter by their finance ministers showed on Monday. In a letter to Ireland, which holds the rotating presidency of the EU, Germany, Spain, Portugal, Italy, Poland and Austria are asking the presidency to put the issue on the agenda of the next EU finance ministers' meeting in Dublin on September 18 to 19. "We are experiencing one of the biggest supply shocks in decades, and all over the world there is growing discontent about the rise in the cost of living," the six finance ministers wrote in the letter, seen by Reuters. "Government measures taken so far have not been sufficient to reduce or stabilise prices for businesses and citizens on a permanent basis. This is why we need a common approach, one that ensures that those who are profiting from the crisis do their part to ease the burden on the general public," they said. Oil prices have risen about 25% from levels at the outbreak of the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran on February 28, while prices of refined products surged more - European diesel prices rose more than 70% since the war began, while gasoline prices have climbed around 20%. "To this end, we need to address the matter of high energy prices by discussing an EU-wide framework to tax windfall profits, taking into account lessons learned in 2022, this time with a more specific analysis of how the foreign profits of multinational oil companies can be included in a more targeted way," the letter said. The ministers also said they wanted to see the results of a European investigation into refiners' margins as soon as possible, to make sure that refineries are not taking advantage of the current energy price spike.

item.content:encoded: Am 35. Jahrestag der Unabhängigkeit der Ukraine ist das Land erneut von Russland attackiert worden. Bei einem russischen Angriff am Stadtrand von Charkiw im Nordosten der Ukraine wurden nach Angaben des regionalen Gouverneurs in der Nacht zum Montag drei Menschen getötet. Nach den Worten von Präsident Wolodymyr Selenskyj strebt die Ukraine ein Ende des Krieges an, ist jedoch nicht bereit, bedingungslos aufzugeben. "Die Ukraine will unbedingt Frieden, doch sie ist nicht bereit, sich einfach zu ergeben", sagte Selenskyj am Montag in einer Rede zum Unabhängigkeitstag in Kiew. Zu den Feierlichkeiten in Kiew wurden unter anderem der britische Premierminister Andy Burnham und EU-Ratspräsident Antonio Costa erwartet. Bundesaußenminister Johann Wadephul hatte bereits am Wochenende die ukrainische Hauptstadt besucht und machte auch Station in Charkiw, das unweit der Front liegt. Zudem war am Montag ein Treffen der sogenannten Koalition der Willigen geplant, an dem auch Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz teilnehmen sollte. Bei dem russischen Angriff in Charkiw gab es auch zahlreiche Verletzte, wie Gouverneur Oleh Synjehubow über den Kurznachrichtendienst Telegram mitteilte. Die Suche nach weiteren möglichen Opfern dauere an. Das ukrainische Militär griff unterdessen nach Angaben des russischen Online-Händlers Ozon vier seiner Logistikzentren im Süden Russlands mit Drohnen an. In einer Anlage in Machatschkala in der Republik Dagestan sei ein Feuer ausgebrochen, teilte der Wildberries-Rivale mit. Ersten Erkenntnissen zufolge seien dort mehrere Menschen verletzt worden. Der Betrieb sei eingestellt worden. In der südrussischen Stadt Krasnodar kamen nach Angaben des örtlichen Gouverneurs zwei Kinder durch herabstürzende Drohnentrümmer ums Leben. Neun weitere Menschen, darunter sieben Kinder, seien verletzt worden, als die Trümmerteile in der Nacht eine private Kindertagesstätte trafen, teilte Gouverneur Wenjamin Kondratjew über den Kurznachrichtendienst Telegram mit. Zudem stürzten Trümmer auf Wohnhäuser und lösten einen Brand in Lagerhallen aus. Auch in der russischen Region Dagestan im Nordkaukasus setzten herabstürzende Drohnentrümmer Lagerhallen in Brand, wie die Nachrichtenagentur Interfax unter Berufung auf regionale Behörden meldete. "SICHERHEIT DER UKRAINE UNSERE SICHERHEIT" Burnham kündigte vor seinem Antrittsbesuch in der Ukraine Unterstützung für die dortige Produktion von Langstreckenraketen an. "Die Sicherheit der Ukraine ist unsere Sicherheit", erklärte Burnham. Großbritannien erlaube dem europäischen Raketenhersteller MBDA, geheime Informationen über britische Bauteile des Marschflugkörpers Scalp weiterzugeben, teilte Burnhams Büro mit. Dies solle Frankreich und der Ukraine helfen, lokale Produktionslinien für die Waffe aufzubauen. Wadephul will nach eigenen Angaben am Montag mit seinem US-Kollegen Marco Rubio telefonieren und ihm Eindrücke seiner jüngsten Reise in die Ukraine schildern. Er wolle Rubio bitten, im Sinne der Ukraine persönlich aktiv zu werden, sagte der CDU-Politiker im Deutschlandfunk. Die US-Diplomatie sei in dieser Hinsicht bisher im Wesentlichen in den Händen der Gesandten Jared Kushner und Steve Witkoff gewesen. "Möglicherweise kann ich ihn (Rubio) selber auch veranlassen, dort noch mehr zu machen, aber wir werden auch auf anderen Wegen versuchen, jetzt Gespräche anzustoßen." "AN DIE GRENZE DES VERANTWORTBAREN" Die EU-Kommission gab unterdessen weitere Finanzhilfen in Höhe von 6,1 Milliarden Euro für die Ukraine frei. Das Geld ist für den Kauf neuer Verteidigungssysteme wie Flugabwehrsysteme, Raketen, Munition und Radargeräte bestimmt, wie die Brüsseler Behörde mitteilte. "Da Russland seine Angriffe intensiviert, verstärken wir unsere Anstrengungen, um der Ukraine beim Schutz ihrer Bevölkerung und bei der Verteidigung ihres Luftraums zu helfen", erklärte EU-Kommissionspräsidentin Ursula von der Leyen. Europa stehe an der Seite der Ukraine und werde liefern, was das Land benötige und wann es dies brauche. Auf den Tag genau seit viereinhalb Jahren wehrt sich die Ukraine mit westlicher Unterstützung gegen den groß angelegten russischen Angriff. Zuletzt hatte die Ukraine verstärkt mit einem Mangel an Munition für Raketenabwehrsysteme zu kämpfen. Wadephul erklärte, er setze sich bei anderen Ländern für die Lieferung von Patriot-Munition ein. "Was die Bundeswehr zur Verfügung gestellt hat, das ging wirklich an die Grenze des Verantwortbaren", so Wadephul. Er habe von Ländern wie Südkorea und Griechenland in dieser Hinsicht weder Zusagen noch Absagen erhalten.

item.title: Indonesia to open airspace for cloud seeding to tackle haze, Malaysia says
item.description: Indonesia has given Malaysian agencies official permission to enter its airspace to conduct cloud seeding operations, Malaysia's environment minister said on Monday, part of both countries' efforts to combat the haze blanketing the region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Indonesia has given Malaysian agencies official permission to enter its airspace to conduct cloud seeding operations, Malaysia's environment minister said on Monday, part of both countries' efforts to combat the haze blanketing the region. Indonesia has been [USN:L1N448068 TEXT:"stepping up"] efforts to slow the spread of haze caused by forest and land fires across several provinces, which this month led to [USN:L6N4490MY TEXT:"dozens of school closures"], including in neighbouring Malaysia. Malaysia's national disaster management agency and its meteorological department were currently preparing schedules for cloud seeding operations in shared border locations, to be coordinated with the Indonesian military, Natural Resources and Environmental Sustainability Minister Arthur Joseph Kurup said in a statement. Malaysia was also prepared to offer assistance to Indonesia in extinguishing fires, with any specific requests to be brought to cabinet for further action, Kurup said. Kurup said the two countries would be escalating their firefighting and fire prevention programmes ahead of national holidays in the coming weeks, including the Malaysia Day celebrations in Sarawak state on September 16. Sarawak, which borders Indonesia's Kalimantan province on Borneo island, has been worst hit by the haze. Six districts in Sarawak recorded unhealthy air pollution index (API) readings on Monday, according to data released by the environment department. Unhealthy API levels were also recorded in eight other districts across four states on the Malaysian peninsula, the data showed.

item.title: Burnham dice que Reino Unido debe ser "más audaz" al buscar vínculos más estrechos con la UE
item.description: El primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, dijo al presidente del Consejo Europeo, António Costa, que Londres debería ser más audaz en la búsqueda de vínculos más estrechos con la Unión Europea y que una cumbre entre Reino Unido y la UE prevista para este año ofrecería una oportunidad para ello, informó el lunes su oficina.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El primer ministro británico, Andy Burnham, dijo al presidente del Consejo Europeo, António Costa, que Londres debería ser más audaz en la búsqueda de vínculos más estrechos con la Unión Europea y que una cumbre entre Reino Unido y la UE prevista para este año ofrecería una oportunidad para ello, informó el lunes su oficina. Burnham se reunió con Costa a última hora del domingo mientras viajaba a Kiev para copresidir una reunión de la denominada "Coalición de los Dispuestos", en su primera visita a Ucrania desde que asumió como primer ministro. Su oficina dijo que Burnham señaló a Costa que Reino Unido debía aprovechar la cooperación ya existente en defensa y seguridad con sus aliados europeos y procurar una colaboración más estrecha en todos los ámbitos de la relación. El líder británico dijo a Costa que Reino Unido "tenía que ser más audaz a la hora de acercarse al bloque", declaró una portavoz de Downing Street sobre las conversaciones entre ambos dirigentes. "Eso incluía aprovechar los estrechos lazos en materia de defensa y seguridad ya forjados entre Reino Unido y sus aliados europeos para impulsar una mayor cooperación en todos los ámbitos de la relación". Reino Unido ha tratado de mejorar sus vínculos comerciales con la UE desde la elección de un Gobierno laborista en 2024, pero los avances han sido lentos y han surgido frustraciones en ambas partes sobre qué debería esperar el antiguo miembro ahora que se encuentra fuera de las principales instituciones. Una portavoz del Gobierno británico dijo que los dos dirigentes coincidieron en que la cumbre entre Reino Unido y la UE prevista para más adelante este año ofrecería una buena plataforma para continuar esa labor. Burnham también se reunió con el primer ministro de Luxemburgo, Luc Frieden, durante su viaje a Kiev. Ambos abordaron distintos mecanismos para aumentar el gasto en defensa, entre ellos el Banco de Defensa, Seguridad y Resiliencia, respaldado por Canadá, y el Mecanismo Multilateral de Defensa puesto en marcha por Reino Unido, Países Bajos, Finlandia y Polonia. Downing Street dijo que los dos dirigentes analizaron cómo podrían complementarse ambos mecanismos.

item.title: Alibaba launches Wan3.0 AI video model after $10 billion share sale
item.description: Alibaba officially rolled out its latest AI video generation-model Wan3.0 on Monday with enhanced capabilities after the Chinese internet giant launched a $10 billion share placement to fund rising AI spending.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Alibaba (9988.HK) officially rolled out its latest AI video generation-model Wan3.0 on Monday with enhanced capabilities after the Chinese internet giant launched a [USN:L6N44L021 TEXT:"$10 billion share placement"] to fund rising AI spending. The new model can generate 30-second videos from documents, spreadsheets, slides and web pages, Alibaba Cloud said in a post on the WeChat platform. Alibaba said Wan3.0 had been used in short drama and film production, advertising and marketing, tourism promotion and music video creation since a public beta version was launched on August 6. The release comes a day after Alibaba announced the share sale, the largest-ever primary follow-on offering by a Hong Kong-listed company, as it ramps up spending in the intensifying global AI race. Alibaba last week [USN:L4N44H0OI TEXT:"reported"] a 75% plunge in quarterly earnings from a year ago due to soaring AI-related capital expenditure.

item.title: India's top factory hub scraps $2.86 billion airport plan, eyes alternative sites
item.description: India's top manufacturing state Tamil Nadu is dropping plans for a second airport to serve its capital Chennai, its chief minister said on Monday, despite calls for expanding aviation capacity to meet the needs of industry.
item.dc:creator: Praveen Paramasivam
item.content:encoded: India's top manufacturing state Tamil Nadu is dropping plans for a second airport to serve its capital Chennai, its chief minister said on Monday, despite calls for expanding aviation capacity to meet the needs of industry. Chennai, dubbed India's Detroit, hosts factories of Hyundai (HYUN.NS) , Renault (RENA.PA) and Apple (AAPL.O) suppliers Foxconn and Tata Electronics. The state has identified alternative locations that will have significantly less impact on agricultural land, Chief Minister Joseph Vijay, who [USN:L4N41J0VX TEXT:"ended a decades-old duopoly"] of two major parties in May, said. The previous government had received civil aviation clearance to develop an airport at Parandur, near Chennai, at an estimated cost of 274 billion rupees ($2.86 billion). The project had faced opposition from farmers. Consultancy Colliers had said the airport would spur demand for industrial parks, air-cargo warehousing and manufacturing facilities nearby. Industry lobby group Confederation of Indian Industry's southern region chairman Ravichandran Purushothaman said it was critical the government swiftly finalise an alternative site and prioritise the project to support Chennai's rapidly expanding industrial, manufacturing, logistics and services sectors. Tamil Nadu accounted for roughly 15% of India's factories and manufacturing employment, the highest among states, according to a federal government statement from a year ago. The state government also plans to expand an existing airport, which handles 30 million passengers a year, to 55 million by upgrading an existing terminal and building a new one. Tamil Nadu signed [USN:L4N44A0CH TEXT:"nearly 100 investment pacts"] worth 674.52 billion rupees in August, including from France's Saint-Gobain (SGOB.PA) , Indian jeweller Titan (TITN.NS) and U.S. server maker Super Micro Computer (SMCI.O) . Die Übungen endeten bereits am vergangenen Freitag. Ursprünglich sollten sie bis zum 27. August gehen. Trump begründete diesen Schritt mit den Kosten und der Weigerung der Regierung in Seoul, sich am Krieg im Iran zu beteiligen. Trumps Vorgehen wurde auch als Signal an Nordkorea angesehen. Damit wolle der US-Präsident den Weg für ein mögliches neues Treffen mit Nordkoreas Machthaber Kim Jong Un bereiten, hieß es aus Südkorea. Ungeachtet des früheren Endes des Manövers feuerte Nordkorea in der vergangenen Woche zehn ballistische Kurzstreckenraketen ab und verurteilte die Übungen. Die Regierung in Pjöngjang kritisiert solche gemeinsamen Militärmanöver seit langem als Proben für eine Invasion.

item.title: Swiss industry fears tariff gap to European Union could hurt US exports
item.description: Swiss industrial companies fear higher tariffs they face on exports to the United States are putting them at a major disadvantage against European rivals who are exposed to lower import charges, a survey said on Monday.
item.dc:creator: John Revill
item.content:encoded: Swiss industrial companies fear higher tariffs they face on exports to the United States are putting them at a major disadvantage against European rivals who are exposed to lower import charges, a survey said on Monday. The U.S. has imposed a [USN:L8N42B0OT TEXT:"tariff rate"] of 12.5% on Swiss goods since the end of July, 2.5 percentage points higher than the duty applied to products from the European Union. A U.S. investigation into industrial overcapacity could result in an even higher tariff rate, further widening the differential with the EU, industry association Swissmem said. "What worries me, aside from the 2.5 percentage point tariff difference compared to the EU, is that the U.S. government is keeping tensions high," said Swissmem chairman Martin Hirzel. According to a Swissmem survey, more than half of Swiss firms are taking a hit on their profit margins rather than passing on the tariffs to their U.S. clients, which they fear losing if they increased prices in line with the import duty. While 42% of companies are able to pass on the increased costs to U.S. customers, Swissmem warned of severe consequences if the current 2.5 percentage point tariff differential with the EU increased further. Hirzel said there was little room for further tariff increases, with U.S.-bound exports already 5.3% down in the first six months of 2026. If the gap increased to 5 percentage points, nearly half of companies said their U.S. business would be seriously endangered, he said. "Companies will not relocate their production to the U.S. as a result, not least because there is a shortage of skilled workers there," Hirzel said. "An agreement that does not put us at a disadvantage relative to our most important competitors remains essential," he added.

item.title: Lions name team to take on All Blacks
item.description: South Africa have released fullback Quan Horn and prop Boan Venter from the Springbok squad to play for provincial side Lions against New Zealand at Ellis Park on Tuesday.

item.content:encoded: South Africa have released fullback Quan Horn and prop Boan Venter from the Springbok squad to play for provincial side Lions against New Zealand at Ellis Park on Tuesday. Venter was named on Monday among the replacements and is in line to make his Lions debut after signing for them, having played for Edinburgh in Scotland. There could also be a debut for former Springbok loose forward Sikhumbuzo Notshe, who previously played club rugby in France and is also on the bench. The Lions’ other Springbok squad member, scrumhalf Morné van den Berg, has not been released, increasing his chances of a run out against the All Blacks in Saturday’s second test in Cape Town. The clash is the last of four games against provincial opposition for the touring All Blacks, who have already beaten the Stormers in Cape Town, Sharks in Durban and Bulls in Pretoria. item.title: Nueva Zelanda presentará un proyecto de ley para prohibir las redes sociales a menores de 16 años
item.description: El primer ministro de Nueva Zelanda, Christopher Luxon, afirmó el lunes que su partido presentará un proyecto de ley en el Parlamento con el objetivo de prohibir el uso de las redes sociales a los menores de 16 años, y propone multas de hasta el 10% de los ingresos globales de una plataforma en caso de incumplimiento.
item.dc:creator: Renju Jose, Alasdair Pal
item.content:encoded: El primer ministro de Nueva Zelanda, Christopher Luxon, afirmó el lunes que su partido presentará un proyecto de ley en el Parlamento con el objetivo de prohibir el uso de las redes sociales a los menores de 16 años, y propone multas de hasta el 10% de los ingresos globales de una plataforma en caso de incumplimiento. El proyecto de ley obligaría a las plataformas de redes sociales a adoptar medidas razonables para verificar la edad de los usuarios, entre otras cosas, utilizando la información existente en las cuentas, la tecnología de reconocimiento facial y los documentos de identidad digitales. "Simplemente no podemos aceptar el daño que se está causando a toda una generación de niños neozelandeses", afirmó Luxon en un comunicado. "Las redes sociales los exponen a contenidos nocivos, a una tecnología adictiva y a presiones para las que no están preparados, y esto está afectando a su vida familiar, su salud mental, su sueño y su educación". No quedó claro de inmediato si el proyecto de ley obtendría el apoyo suficiente para ser aprobado en el Parlamento, ya que uno de los socios de la coalición de Luxon, el partido New Zealand First, ha declarado que no lo respaldará. "Nos preocupa la legislación propuesta, así como la dirección y la pendiente resbaladiza hacia la que, inevitablemente, llevará a nuestro país una ley como esta", dijo el líder de New Zealand First, Winston Peters —que también es ministro de Asuntos Exteriores del país— en una publicación en la red social X. En diciembre, Australia se convirtió en el primer país del mundo en prohibir las redes sociales a los menores de 16 años, impidiéndoles el acceso a plataformas como TikTok, Youtube de Alphabet (GOOGL.O) , e Instagram y Facebook de Meta (META.O) . Esa legislación había sido un "fracaso colosal", afirmó Peters, y añadió que mantener a los menores alejados de las redes sociales debería ser responsabilidad de los padres. "No voy a fingir que va a ser sencillo ni que va a ser perfecto", dijo Luxon en un acto. "No conseguiremos que todos y cada uno de los niños dejen de usar las redes sociales. Algunos siempre encontrarán la manera de eludir las restricciones, pero, francamente, es demasiado importante como para no intentarlo al menos".

item.title: EZB-Direktor: Europas Wirtschaft trotz Iran-Krieg überraschend robust
item.description: EZB-Direktor Piero Cipollone geht nicht davon aus, dass Europas Wirtschaft wegen der Krise um die für den Öltransport wichtige Straße von Hormus in eine Flaute gepaart mit hoher Inflation gerät. Es gebe Anzeichen dafür, dass die Krise bald beigelegt werden könnte, und selbst der Ölpreis scheine dies widerzuspiegeln, sagte Cipollone. Die jüngsten verfügbaren Daten deuteten zwar darauf hin, dass die europäische Wirtschaft an Schwung verliere. Trotz der konjunkturellen Abkühlung erweise sie sich jedoch als überraschend widerstandsfähig.

item.title: Las acciones europeas bajan por el lastre del sector tecnológico
item.description: Las bolsas europeas bajaban ligeramente el lunes, lastradas por los valores tecnológicos, mientras los inversionistas esperaban los detalles de las sanciones que Estados Unidos había amenazado con imponer a Irán, y que se darían a conocer más adelante en la sesión.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Las bolsas europeas bajaban ligeramente el lunes, lastradas por los valores tecnológicos, mientras los inversionistas esperaban los detalles de las sanciones que Estados Unidos había amenazado con imponer a Irán, y que se darían a conocer más adelante en la sesión. El índice paneuropeo STOXX 600 (.STOXX) bajaba un 0,1%, hasta los 653,40 puntos, a las 0713 GMT. Estados Unidos amenazó a Irán con lo que calificó como "la mayor ofensiva financiera jamás organizada", mientras se preparaba para poner en marcha sanciones económicas dirigidas a los socios comerciales de Teherán, mientras que Irán prometió bloquear todas las exportaciones de petróleo del golfo Pérsico "si la guerra económica continúa". Las acciones del sector energético (.SXEP) caían un 0,4%, siguiendo la tendencia de los precios del crudo Brent , que se situaban en torno a los 92 dólares por barril. En el lado positivo, el sector de los recursos básicos (.SXPP) era el que mejor se comportaba, con una subida del 0,8%, tras el repunte de los precios del oro ante la debilidad del dólar. Mientras tanto, el sector tecnológico (.SX8P) se mostraba nervioso a la espera de los resultados de Nvidia (NVDA.O) del miércoles, en un momento en que los inversionistas eran conscientes de lo difícil que será para el fabricante de chips cumplir con unas expectativas estratosféricas. Los participantes en el mercado también esperarán obtener claridad sobre las perspectivas de las tasas de interés estadounidenses cuando el presidente de la Reserva Federal, Kevin Warsh, intervenga en Jackson Hole, Wyoming, el viernes, un evento que se seguirá con atención en busca de nuevas pistas.

item.content:encoded: China's foreign ministry said on Monday Beijing will closely watch developments and do what is necessary to protect its rights as the U.S. prepares to [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"unveil new Iran sanctions"] that are expected to target Tehran's trading partners. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent, who is set to hold a press conference at 1 p.m. EDT (1700 GMT) on Monday, has threatened to impose "the toughest sanctions in history" on Iran and urged China to cooperate with Washington. item.title: Un ataque con drones mata a tres adolescentes en la ciudad rusa de Krasnodar
item.description: Tres adolescentes fallecieron y otras ocho personas, entre ellas siete niños, resultaron heridas después de que los restos de un dron impactaran durante la noche en una guardería privada de la región de Krasnodar, en el sur de Rusia, según las autoridades rusas.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tres adolescentes fallecieron y otras ocho personas, entre ellas siete niños, resultaron heridas después de que los restos de un dron impactaran durante la noche en una guardería privada de la región de Krasnodar, en el sur de Rusia, según las autoridades rusas. En una publicación en la aplicación de mensajería Telegram, la comisionada rusa para los derechos del niño, María Lvova-Belova, afirmó que tres adolescentes, de 13, 15 y 16 años, habían fallecido, y que otros seis niños habían sido hospitalizados. El gobernador local, Veniamín Kondrátiev, señaló que también resultaron heridos dos adultos. Kondrátiev declaró en un comunicado en Telegram que las muertes se habían producido después de que los restos de un dron impactaran contra una guardería privada en la ciudad de Krasnodar. No hubo comentarios inmediatos por parte de Kiev. El ataque se produjo mientras Ucrania atacaba varios centros logísticos pertenecientes al minorista en línea ruso Ozon, entre ellos uno situado en la localidad de Enem, cerca de la ciudad de Krasnodar. Ozon afirmó que también había evacuado almacenes en las regiones vecinas de Adigueya y Stávropol, mientras que otro almacén en Daguestán había sido objeto de un ataque. Ucrania ha intensificado los ataques contra centros logísticos y almacenes en toda Rusia, lo que acerca la guerra que Moscú inició en febrero de 2022 a los rusos de a pie, algunos de los cuales se ganan la vida vendiendo productos por internet. En unas declaraciones publicadas el sábado, el presidente ruso, Vladimir Putin, afirmó que Kiev había abierto una "caja de Pandora" con sus ataques contra objetivos económicos rusos y que Moscú respondería golpeando los "sectores económicos más sensibles" de Ucrania. Tanto Rusia como Ucrania niegan haber atacado deliberadamente a civiles. Según las Naciones Unidas, más de 16.000 civiles han perdido la vida en casi cuatro años y medio de combates, la inmensa mayoría de ellos ucranianos.

item.title: India's Godrej Industries group signs pact to invest $2 billion in Haryana state
item.description: India's Godrej Industries group on Monday said it has signed a pact with the government of Haryana to invest 200 billion rupees ($2.09 billion) in the northern state, expanding its presence in the region.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's Godrej Industries group on Monday said it has signed a pact with the government of Haryana to invest 200 billion rupees ($2.09 billion) in the northern state, expanding its presence in the region. The group has signed a memorandum of understanding with the state government with the investment expected to create around 40,000 jobs. Godrej Industries Group, which operates across consumer goods, real estate and financial services, has invested about 120 billion rupees in Haryana so far and employs around 9,000 people in the state. The group posted revenue of $7.2 billion in fiscal 2026. Godrej Properties (GODR.NS) , the group's real estate arm, will be a key driver of the investment and plans to deploy a further 160 billion rupees in Haryana by fiscal 2028, taking its total investment in the state to around 270 billion rupees. Godrej Ventures, the group's real estate private equity business, plans to invest another 35 billion rupees in office infrastructure in Gurugram. The proposed investment is expected to generate more than 30,000 direct and indirect jobs, it said. "Haryana has emerged as an important growth driver for the Godrej Industries Group," Chairperson Pirojsha Godrej said, adding that the group sees the region as a market where it can continue to invest for the long term. ($1 = 95.7250 Indian rupees)

item.title: California cancels talks with Paramount over Warner Bros merger, NYT reports
item.description: California's Attorney General Rob Bonta canceled a meeting with Paramount Skydance representatives scheduled for Monday to begin settlement talks over the state's lawsuit seeking to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery , the New York Times reported.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: California's Attorney General Rob Bonta canceled a meeting with Paramount Skydance (PSKY.O) representatives scheduled for Monday to begin settlement talks over the state's lawsuit seeking to block Paramount's proposed acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery (WBD.O) , the New York Times reported. Citing a statement from Bonta's office, the newspaper said he accused Paramount of leaking details of a meeting held on Friday and acting in bad faith. Here are some details: “Not only did Paramount leak the alleged substance of settlement discussions, but they misrepresented these discussions, demonstrating a lack of good faith,” the report said, citing the statement. Paramount and the California Attorney General's office did not respond to Reuters requests for comment outside regular business hours. The New York Times [USN:L6N44J066 TEXT:"reported"] on Saturday talks between the two parties were preliminary, and there was no assurance that they will lead to meaningful negotiations toward a settlement. Last month, California and 11 states [USN:L6N43G09L TEXT:"sued"] to block Paramount's $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros. Discovery, alleging the deal would lessen competition in film distribution and cable television, harming theaters and pay TV distributors. States including New York, Arizona and Minnesota argued the deal would harm theaters and television distributors, raise prices for consumers and make wages less competitive for workers. (This story has been refiled to correct spacing in paragraph 1.)

item.title: European shares steady on Iran sanctions uncertainty
item.description: European shares were little changed on Monday as higher gold prices lent support, though uncertainty surrounding impending U.S. sanctions on Iran kept risk appetite in check.
item.dc:creator: Tharuniyaa Lakshmi
item.content:encoded: European shares were little changed on Monday as higher gold prices lent support, though uncertainty surrounding impending U.S. sanctions on Iran kept risk appetite in check. The pan-European STOXX 600 (.STOXX) was up 0.03% at 654.38 points, as of 0837 GMT. Basic Resources (.SXPP) rose 0.7% as gold prices climbed on a weaker dollar. Travel and Leisure (.SXTP) was the top-performing sector, rising 1% as lower oil prices boosted sentiment towards the energy-sensitive sector. The [USN:L6N44K07T TEXT:"U.S. threatened Iran"] with what it called "the greatest financial offensive ever marshalled" as it prepared to roll out economic sanctions targeting Iran's trade partners, while Iran vowed to shut down all oil exports from the Gulf "if the economic war continues." Energy shares (.SXEP) were the worst-performing sector, falling 0.6%, tracking Brent crude prices , which were at around $93 a barrel. Automobiles and parts (.SXAP) fell 0.5%, despite data showing [USN:L1N44A0H2 TEXT:"European EV sales picked up"] in July. The European benchmark ended lower last week as higher oil prices, rising U.S. bond yields and escalating Middle East tensions stoked inflation concerns, prompting investors to price in a more hawkish path for central banks including the European Central Bank. Money markets are pricing in a more [USN:L1N44L06D TEXT:"hawkish ECB"], betting geopolitical tensions could keep price pressures elevated and drive the deposit rate close to 3% by late 2027. Investors are also looking ahead to the central bank's September meeting after policymakers tightened policy in June following an energy shock linked to the U.S.-Iran conflict. Market participants will also be hoping for clarity on the U.S. interest rate outlook when Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh speaks in Jackson Hole, Wyoming, on Friday. "Warsh has been opposed to expanding balance sheet which takes away one of the support measures for the long end. Warsh is likely to focus on credibility and emphasize that the Fed is ready to act on inflation to control the long end of the curve," Mohit Kumar at Jefferies said =. Meanwhile, the tech sector (.SX8P) was on edge ahead of Nvidia's (NVDA.O) results on Wednesday, with investors worried that it would be difficult for the chipmaker to meet stratospheric expectations.

item.title: Iran warns vessels violating Hormuz transit rules of fines, detention
item.description: The warning heightens risks for charterers and shipowners.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Iran has issued a warning that vessels violating its arrangements for transiting the Strait of Hormuz could face restrictions, including fines, detention, or confiscation, the Persian Gulf Strait Authority wrote in a post on X. The warning heightens risks for the charterers and shipowners whose vessels transit through the Strait of Hormuz, a key waterway for the world's energy shipments. The PGSA, a new body Iran has established with the aim of managing the strait, has said cargo owners should refer to an updated list of vessels deemed non-compliant for voyages relating to the Persian Gulf. Vessels engaging in operations including ship-to-ship transfers or transshipment with non-compliant vessels will also be added to the restricted list, it said. Ships seeking the removal of their names from the non-compliant vessels' list must submit a request with relevant explanations to Iran's maritime authorities, the post said.

item.title: Scentre to sell half of Queensland shopping centre for $632 mln
item.description: Scentre Group said on Monday Australian Retirement Trust will acquire a 50% stake in its Queensland shopping centre Westfield Mt Gravatt for A$882.5 million ($632.22 million), a 3.5% premium to the property's December 2025 book value.
item.dc:creator: Kumar Tanishk
item.content:encoded: Scentre Group (SCG.AX) said on Monday Australian Retirement Trust will acquire a 50% stake in its Queensland shopping centre Westfield Mt Gravatt for A$882.5 million ($632.22 million), a 3.5% premium to the property's December 2025 book value. Here are some other details: Over the past 13 months, Scentre has attracted A$3.1 billion in third-party capital by forming joint ventures around its assets under a long-term plan. The Queensland shopping centre attracted more than 17 million customer visits in the prior year and generated business partner sales exceeding A$1 billion, Scentre said. The group will retain management responsibilities. The deal includes the sale of a 50% direct property stake for A$870 million based on a 5.50% property yield and a 50% stake in adjacent land for A$12.5 million. Selling assets at sub-cost-of-capital yields is value-accretive, while retaining a 50% stake and full-property fee streams preserves meaningful exposure and unlocks capital for higher-value redeployment, said Emanuel Ajay Datt, MD of Datt Group. "We expect this transaction will firm up Scentre's ability to distribute income to shareholders," Datt said. The trust had [USN:L4N3XT06Y TEXT:"acquired"] a nearly 20% interest in Scentre’s flagship Westfield Sydney mall for A$864 million last year. Peer Vicinity (VCX.AX) , which owns centres including Queen Victoria Building in Sydney, has also been active in acquisitions. In May 2026, it [USN:TUEBWYJ0S TEXT:"purchased "]Eastern Creek Quarter in western Sydney from Frasers Property (FRPL.SI) for A$400 million. Scentre shares have traded in a range of A$3.28 to A$4.24 over the past year and have fallen more than 13% from their January peak. Its shares closed flat on the day. ($1 = 1.3959 Australian dollars)

item.title: Thames Water's creditors line up new board under proposed rescue deal
item.description: Thames Water's senior creditors on Monday named the first group of proposed directors, including a turnaround specialist and a former civil servant, to oversee a decade-long overhaul of Britain's struggling utility if its rescue plan is approved.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Thames Water's senior creditors on Monday named the first group of proposed directors, including a turnaround specialist and a former civil servant, to oversee a decade-long overhaul of Britain's struggling utility if its rescue plan is approved. Britain's largest water supplier, saddled with about £20 billion ($27 billion) in debt, has been fighting for survival after successive owners failed to invest adequately in its ageing infrastructure. The company has also faced public anger over sewage discharges into rivers. The senior creditor consortium, known as London & Valley Water, in July proposed a revised [USN:L4N43N0D6 TEXT:"rescue plan"] that includes a 10-year transformation programme and a possible 'golden share' for the government in an effort to avoid the company being taken into public ownership under Prime Minister Andy Burnham's government. The plan aims to invest in Thames Water’s infrastructure and address the root cause of critical issues such as pollution and leakage. The appointments hinge on the approval of the turnaround plan, water regulator Ofwat clearing each director, and a new capital structure being put in place through a court-sanctioned restructuring. The creditors, holding £17 billion of the troubled utility's debt, proposed installing broadband network Openreach's chair Mike McTighe, former Yorkshire Water CEO Liz Barber, ex-CEO of Openreach Clive Selley and former Permanent Secretary at the Department for Transport, Bernadette Kelly, to Thames Water's board. “It will take time to fix Thames Water, but we are committed to rebuilding trust with the customers and public Thames Water serves,” said McTighe, who would lead the governance overhaul and build the new Thames Water board. Collectively, the group of directors has experience in turning around businesses and running regulated utilities in Britain. “Thames Water continues to work constructively to reach an agreement that supports its long-term financial stability," a spokesperson for the utility said in an emailed statement to Reuters. ($1 = £0.7331)

item.title: Volkswagen workers criticise board's communication
item.description: Volkswagen employees have criticised what they called the management board's "disastrous external communication" as Europe's largest automaker considers further cost cuts.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Volkswagen (VOWG.DE) employees have criticised what they called the management board's "disastrous external communication" as Europe's largest automaker considers [USN:L8N44I0TG TEXT:"further cost cuts"], according to an internal works council article seen by Reuters on Monday. An online survey, conducted last week by Volkswagen's Group works council, found that employees and their families were "unsettled and frightened" by the board's public communication, the article said. Employees also raised concerns about job security, the future of early-retirement and severance programmes, and prospects for Volkswagen's plants in Emden, Hanover, Neckarsulm, Osnabrueck and Zwickau. In [USN:L8N44I0TG TEXT:"an internal company memo on Friday"], CEO Oliver Blume said four of those plants were not expected to reach competitive capacity utilisation in the 2030s, but stressed that there was no decision yet on specific plant closures. The workers criticised the lack of details on the future of these plants provided on Friday. Blume has rejected accusations of withholding information. "We continuously keep our colleagues and employee representatives informed about the status of the plans—through internal channels, but above all through direct personal dialogue," he said in July in an interview published on the company's website. Volkswagen is undergoing what is considered to be its largest-ever restructuring, possibly ranging from a further [USN:L8N42Y0CC TEXT:"50,000 job cuts"] to the [USN:L8N42Y1AR TEXT:"carve-out of some divisions"]. Blume will address employees at an extraordinary meeting in Wolfsburg on Tuesday and Thomas Schmall, head of components and a member of the management board, will speak in Braunschweig. The works council called the meetings in July after employee representatives criticised the management's communication over plans to improve the automaker's competitiveness.

item.title: Taiwan issues indictments over alleged illegal export of AI servers to China
item.description: Taiwan prosecutors said on Monday they had indicted nine people, including employees of Nvidia and Super Micro , over involvement in the illegal export of artificial intelligence servers to China.
item.dc:creator: Wen-Yee Lee, Ben Blanchard
item.content:encoded: Taiwan prosecutors said on Monday they had indicted nine people, including employees of Nvidia (NVDA.O) and Super Micro (SMCI.O) , over involvement in the illegal export of artificial intelligence servers to China. Semiconductor powerhouse Taiwan is the world's largest producer of advanced chips used in AI applications. Prosecutors [USN:P8N42I0AL TEXT:"this year"] investigated the suspected illegal export of servers equipped with Nvidia chips subject to U.S. export controls. Washington has imposed curbs since 2022 making it illegal for such semiconductors to be exported or sold in China without a license. Eight people, including one employee of Nvidia's Taiwan unit and two employees of Super Micro's Taiwan unit, were charged with breach of trust and document forgery in connection with the illegal export of high-end AI servers, prosecutors in the port city of Keelung said in a statement. Neither company immediately responded to requests for comment. A ninth defendant was charged in a related case involving the alleged siphoning of funds from a distributor company involved, the statement said, without providing the full names of any of the defendants. The alleged scheme involved making it appear that 130 B300 servers ordered from Super Micro would be installed and used at a rented server facility in Taiwan. Prosecutors said false end-user documents stated that the servers would be installed in Taiwan. Of those 130 servers, 74 were ultimately exported and delivered to Chinese customers through routes that included direct shipments to China as well as transhipments through Indonesia, Japan and Hong Kong, they said. The remaining 56 servers were intended to be exported to a company in Japan, prosecutors said, but Taiwan customs officials detected irregularities and stopped their export. 'FULLY AWARE' OF CONTROLS The prosecutors said the defendants were "fully aware" that both Nvidia and Super Micro have "rigorous internal control procedures" regarding exports. However, the defendants "colluded with one another at various levels for enormous profit, illegally exporting high-end servers, increasing corporate compliance costs, and severely damaging our nation's international image", they added. Taiwan has tightened export controls in recent years to keep advanced technology and know-how from reaching China, which claims the democratically governed island as its own territory despite the strong objections of the island's government.

item.title: US refiners face historic stress test as global crisis looms
item.description: U.S. refineries have operated near maximum capacity for the longest sustained period in over a quarter century, scrambling to capture windfall profits created by the Iran war. But history offers a cautionary tale: “Super refining” runs that push plants too hard can cause major failures.
item.dc:creator: Ron Bousso
item.content:encoded: U.S. refineries have operated near maximum capacity for the longest sustained period in over a quarter century, scrambling to capture windfall profits created by the [USN:L8N44H1WH TEXT:"Iran war"]. But history offers a cautionary tale: “Super refining” runs that push plants too hard can cause major failures. This has global implications. U.S. refineries’ ability to sustain today’s elevated operating rates for months, or potentially years, could mean the difference between an exceptionally tight global fuel market and a full-blown supply crisis marked by acute shortages, demand destruction and widespread economic pain. A U.S.-Israeli air campaign against Iran in late February triggered the closure of the [USN:L6N44E0UW TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"], [USN:L4N44I05C TEXT:"disrupting"] a fifth of global oil supply and severely hampering refining operations, particularly in Asia. Meanwhile, relentless Ukrainian attacks on Russian refineries caused Moscow to suspend diesel exports in July. The result has been [USN:L6N44G0ZC TEXT:"a collapse"] in global fuel production. Global refinery throughput in July fell to 81 million barrels per day (bpd), nearly 5 million bpd, or about 6%, below the level at this point last year, according to the International Energy Agency (IEA). The U.S., the world's largest crude producer and second-largest refiner after China, responded by ramping up exports of [USN:L1N41C0XB TEXT:"crude"], [USN:L1N40K11P TEXT:"gasoline, diesel and jet fuel"] to record levels, according to the U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA), helping avert a truly cataclysmic supply shock. For the U.S. refining industry, the past six months have been an unprecedented bonanza. Benchmark margins for converting crude into transportation fuels have averaged more than $50 a barrel since the start of the war, more than double their 10-year average. As a result, major U.S. refiners including [USN:L4N43W0YL TEXT:"Valero"] (VLO.N) , [USN:L4N442125 TEXT:"Phillips 66"] (PSX.N) , [USN:L4N4410TR TEXT:"Marathon Petroleum"] (MPC.N) and [USN:L6N43Q18H TEXT:"Exxon Mobil"] (XOM.N) posted record or near-record second-quarter earnings. To generate those bumper profits, many companies postponed planned maintenance and kept plants running at full tilt. U.S. refinery throughput has averaged around 17 million bpd since the start of the conflict, significantly above its five-year average. The question now is how long this can last before something breaks. PARTY LIKE IT’S 1997 This period of sustained maximum production has few precedents in modern history. Over the past 11 weeks, U.S. refinery utilisation rates have hovered above 95% — a sustained level not seen in more than 25 years. In fact, refineries have only achieved such prolonged rates three times, based on EIA data going back to 1990. The closest parallels came in 1997 and 1998, when U.S. refineries recorded two separate 24-week stretches of utilisation rates above 95% — first between May and October 1997 and again between April and September 1998. In the summer of 1998, the refinery fleet exceeded 100% utilisation – the only time this has occurred in EIA records. That extraordinary performance was driven by a rare combination of low crude prices and consistently strong fuel demand, giving refiners every incentive to keep operations running flat out. A similar episode followed in 2000, when refineries operated above 95% utilisation for 13 consecutive weeks, but the conditions were markedly different. The Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries had introduced production cuts in 1999 that caused crude prices to nearly double by mid-2000. While this squeezed refinery profit margins, it coincided with the early stages of the China-driven commodities super-cycle, when global fuel demand skyrocketed, forcing refineries to run hard to meet it. The rally ultimately ended as crude became too expensive to sustain such high operating rates. The current episode looks quite different from any of these precedents. Today's utilisation surge is being driven not by cheap feedstock or runaway demand but by a severe shortage of refining capacity caused by war-related damage in Iran and Russia. But those episodes illustrate the risk refiners are taking. A DANGEROUS PRECIPICE Running complex refining systems at breakneck speeds for extended periods inevitably increases the risk of equipment failures, accidents and unplanned outages. Faced with soaring margins and a global fuel shortage, many U.S. refiners have deferred essential maintenance originally scheduled for the second quarter, pushing much of the work into late 2026 or even 2027. The risk is that doing this could ultimately lead to sharp, unplanned capacity losses. History offers mixed lessons. The first super-refining episode in 1997 ended relatively gradually, with utilisation easing from above 95% in mid-October to around 92% a month later before quickly rebounding. The reckoning came the following year. After the 24-week run in 1998, utilisation plunged from around 95% in late September to 86% by mid-October as several refineries were forced into emergency maintenance after months of operating at full capacity. A similar pattern emerged in 2018, when an eight-week period of utilisation above 95% was followed by a rapid drop to 89% within weeks. The 2000 rally was the notable exception, as it ended without a comparable collapse. So what’s the risk of a breakdown this time? On the one hand, the industry today has a far better understanding of the risks associated with prolonged periods of elevated utilisation. Yet today’s global refining crisis is unlike anything refiners have ever faced. Fuel inventories are being depleted, while severe damage to refining infrastructure in the Middle East and Russia is likely to leave the world with reduced processing capacity for years. The risk of losing further capacity is greater than at any time in the recent past because global refining output is nearly 2 million bpd below demand, according to the IEA. That creates a dangerous dilemma. The longer refining margins remain elevated, the greater the temptation for refiners to keep running flat out. But the harder they run, the greater the risk of failures that could remove even more fuel from an already stretched market. For now, America's refiners are serving as the world's supplier of last resort. The danger is that the world has become so dependent on them that even a small disruption to their operations could tip an already fragile market into a genuine fuel crisis.
